cluster_summary: Multiple endpoints across different modules accept state-changing HTTP requests (POST, GET with side effects) without requiring a per-request CSRF token. Attackers can forge cross-origin requests that execute actions using the victim's authenticated session. Fixes involve generating a unique token, embedding it in forms or as a header, and validating it server-side before processing.
guideline_text: Trace lower-privilege script, template, macro, plugin, or API callers that can invoke privileged server-side capabilities into server-side include, template rendering, servlet dispatch, raw object access, internal file reads, or privileged framework APIs. Report code paths where a higher privilege check is not enforced at the API entry point before exposing the server-side capability. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should check the required higher privilege at the exposed API boundary and return no sensitive result when the caller lacks that privilege.

mechanism.missing_guard: a higher privilege check is not enforced at the API entry point before exposing the server-side capability
mechanism.name: privileged server-side capability exposed to lower privilege context
mechanism.sink_shape: server-side include, template rendering, servlet dispatch, raw object access, internal file reads, or privileged framework APIs
mechanism.source_shape: lower-privilege script, template, macro, plugin, or API callers that can invoke privileged server-side capabilities
mechanism.typical_fix: check the required higher privilege at the exposed API boundary and return no sensitive result when the caller lacks that privilege

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add server-side CSRF token generation and validation: embed a unique token as a hidden field in forms or as a custom header (e.g., X-CSRF-Token), and reject any request where the token is missing, invalid, or mismatched with the session. Use existing framework CSRF services (e.g., `$services.csrf.isTokenValid()`) to enforce the check before processing the action.
sub_patterns.name: missing CSRF token validation on state-changing endpoints
sub_patterns.root_cause: The application does not generate or validate a unique anti-CSRF token (nonce) for HTTP requests that perform state-changing operations (e.g., creating, updating, deleting resources, executing scheduler actions). The server trusts that any authenticated request is intentional, lacking a mechanism to distinguish legitimate user actions from forged cross-site requests.

sub_patterns.name: missing anti-CSRF token validation on state-changing operations
